builds.title: Sill, Shadow Fighter 1
builds.languages: Understands, reads and writes Common. Cannot speak.
traits: Proficiency +2. Strength and Constitution saves both +4. AC 13 is 10 + Dexterity 3. Hit points are 10 + Constitution 2. Sill carries a shortsword and wears no armor or shield.
Fighter grants Acrobatics and Athletics. Criminal grants Deception, Stealth and a contact, here a lamp trimmer who works the south gate.
Undead. Immune to poison damage, exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned and restrained. In sunlight, attacks, checks and saves have disadvantage.
Sill fits through a 1-inch gap without squeezing and writes messages in dust. Four hours of semiconscious rest replace sleep. Short-rest Hit Dice and ordinary long-rest healing work.
actions: Strength Drain. Melee unarmed attack +4 within 5 ft. for 1d8 + 2 necrotic. A natural 20 against a living creature also forces a DC 12 Strength save. First failure gives disadvantage on Strength attacks, checks and saves until a short or long rest or lesser restoration or similar magic. Another natural 20 while drained allows another save. On failure the target drops to 0 HP and starts dying.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack +5 within 5 ft. for 1d6 + 5 piercing. Includes Dexterity and the +2 damage from Dueling.
Shadow Stealth. Hide as a bonus action in dim light or darkness.
Second Wind. Regain 1d10 + 1 HP as a bonus action once per short or long rest.
builds.tactics: Sill writes warnings before approaching. If someone draws a blade, Sill circles through a crack and tries to reach cover. In an open fight Sill uses Strength Drain on a living pursuer and keeps Second Wind for a retreat.

builds.title: Bramble-Eye, Blood Hawk Rogue 2
builds.senses: Passive Perception 16, or 21 on sight tasks where Keen Sight applies.
traits: Proficiency +2. Dexterity save +5. Intelligence save +3. AC 13 is 10 + Dexterity 3 while unarmored. HP is 10 at level 1 plus 7 at level 2 using the fixed gain.
Rogue grants Acrobatics, Insight, Perception and Stealth, with Expertise in Perception and Stealth. Folk Hero grants Animal Handling and Survival.
Keen Sight grants advantage on visual Perception. No Hands bars wielded weapons, shields and tool use. Bramble-Eye travels without equipment.
actions: Bite. Melee unarmed attack +5 within 5 ft. for 1d4 + 3 slashing. Add 1d6 slashing once per turn if the attack qualifies for Sneak Attack.
Sneak Attack. The finesse bite qualifies with advantage, or if another enemy is within 5 ft. of the target, that enemy is not incapacitated, and the attack has no disadvantage.
Pack Tactics. Bonus action. The next attack this turn has advantage if a non-incapacitated ally is within 5 ft. of the target.
Cunning Action. Bonus-action Dash, Disengage or Hide. Choose this or Pack Tactics on a given turn.
builds.tactics: Bramble-Eye scouts from above. If a partner corners the poacher, Bramble-Eye dives to bite. Without support, Bramble-Eye uses Cunning Action to leave melee and keep watch from a roof.

builds.title: Copper Sedge, Flying Snake Monk 1
builds.speed: 30 ft. walking, 30 ft. swimming, 30 ft. flying
traits: Proficiency +2. Strength save +1. Dexterity save +5. AC 15 is 10 + Dexterity 3 + Wisdom 2 from Unarmored Defense. HP is 8 + Constitution 2.
Monk grants Acrobatics and Insight. Hermit grants Medicine, Religion and Elvish. Copper Sedge has no gear it needs to handle.
Serpentine Body prevents armor, shields, weapons and manipulated items. Copper Sedge has blindsight within 10 ft. Flight uses normal opportunity-attack and falling rules.
actions: Bite. Melee unarmed attack +5 within 5 ft. for 1d4 + 3 piercing plus 1d4 poison. Use Dexterity for the attack and apply its damage bonus to piercing.
Martial Arts tail slap. After using the Attack action for an unarmed strike, make one conventional unarmed strike as a bonus action. Melee attack +5 within 5 ft. for 1d4 + 3 bludgeoning.
builds.tactics: Copper Sedge swims low beside the barge and watches the mooring. If a thief closes in, Copper Sedge bites and follows with a tail slap, then flies away when it can leave reach safely.

builds.title: Thimbleback, Giant Centipede Rogue 1
builds.languages: Common. Dwarvish from Outlander. Thieves’ cant from Rogue.
traits: Proficiency +2. Dexterity save +5. Intelligence save +3. Natural Armor AC 14 is 11 + Dexterity 3. HP is 8 + Constitution 2.
Rogue grants Acrobatics, Investigation, Perception and Stealth, with Expertise in Perception and Stealth. Outlander grants Athletics, Survival and Dwarvish.
No Hands bars wielded weapons, shields and tools. The climb speed uses ordinary climbing rules and grants no special hold on ceilings.
actions: Bite. Melee unarmed attack +5 within 5 ft. for 1d4 + 3 piercing plus 1d4 poison. Once per turn, add 1d6 piercing when the bite qualifies for Sneak Attack.
Sneak Attack. The finesse bite qualifies with advantage, or if another enemy is within 5 ft. of the target, that enemy is not incapacitated, and the attack has no disadvantage.
Hide. Use an action to attempt Stealth +7 when the situation permits.
builds.tactics: Thimbleback guides visitors through a ventilation crawl and stops when it senses movement ahead. In a fight it bites from concealment or while a companion holds the entrance.

concepts.name: Sill
concepts.motive: Find the lamp trimmer before the next gate shift.
concepts.hook: A charcoal arrow appears beneath the watch ledger every night. Tonight it points at a name someone has scraped out.

concepts.name: Bramble-Eye
concepts.motive: Drive a poacher away from the breeding ground.
concepts.hook: Bramble-Eye can follow a particular snare-maker by sight. The hawk asks the party to walk the ditch below and cut the first snare it finds.

concepts.name: Copper Sedge
concepts.motive: Get a missing ferry back to the landing.
concepts.hook: Copper Sedge watched a barge go upriver with its rope still trailing. It wants someone with hands to find out who cut it loose.

concepts.name: Thimbleback
concepts.motive: Keep an apprentice from opening a sealed culvert.
concepts.hook: Thimbleback heard hammering through a bricked-up culvert and learned enough Dwarvish to know the rhythm means keep out.
